title: Simple Present Tense
subtitle: The tense for habits, facts and things happening right now on screen.
objectives: Form the simple present tense, including the third person singular
Apply the spelling rules for adding -s or -es
Explain the four main uses of the simple present
Form negatives and questions using do and does
Retell the episode with the monks and the coach

cards.title: The tense you use most and think about least
cards.text: It is the base form of the verb, with one change for he, she and it. That one change is where all the marks are.

cards.title: Only the third person singular changes
cards.text: Five of the six forms are just the plain verb. The odd one out is he, she or it.
points: **I walk · you walk · we walk · they walk.**
**Forgetting the -s** is the most marked error at this level.

cards.title: When it is -s and when it is -es
cards.text: Six rules. Tap through — two quiz questions come from these.

question.text: What is the correct third person form of "watch"?
question.explain: Verbs ending in -ch take -es, because -s alone would be unsayable.

cards.title: It depends on the letter before the y
cards.text: This is the rule that separates the people who learned it from the people who guessed.
points: **Consonant + y:** change y to i, add -es. *carry → carries*
**Vowel + y:** keep the y, add -s. *play → plays*
**Look at the letter before the y.**

question.text: Write the third person singular of "study".
question.explain: Consonant before the y, so the y becomes i and -es is added: studies.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: Forming it is done. Part 2 is what it is for, and the monks. Your place is saved.

cards.title: Four jobs, and one of them surprises people
cards.text: Habits and facts are the obvious two. The other two are why sports commentary and stage directions sound the way they do.

cards.title: What the simple present is for
cards.text: These are the four the exam asks about. The last two are the ones students never think of.

cards.title: Every race commentary is in the present tense
cards.text: "He goes wide, he takes the inside line, he holds it." All happening now, all in the simple present.
points: **Not "he went wide."** That is a report afterwards.
**It is a deliberate choice**, not an accident.

question.text: "The train leaves at 7:15." Which use is this?
question.explain: A fixed schedule. English uses the simple present for these even though the event is in the future.

cards.title: A training plan is written in the present tense
cards.text: Not "you will warm up" but "you warm up, you shadow box, you spar". It reads as what happens, not what might.
points: **A habit is stated as a fact.**
**"He is training"** means right this second.

cards.title: Do and does take the -s so the main verb does not
cards.text: Once you add do or does, the main verb goes back to its plain form. This is where the double -s error happens.

cards.title: Every tooltip is in the simple present
cards.text: "This weapon deals extra damage. The potion restores health." Nothing is being described as happening once.
points: **That is why they read as rules.**

question.explain: Does carries the -s, so like goes back to its plain form. Only one word takes the ending.

cards.title: The Adventure with the Monks
cards.text: Two monks on mules come down the road, and behind them a coach carrying a lady. Don Quixote reads the scene instantly and wrongly.

cards.title: Enchanters carrying off a princess
cards.text: The monks are travellers minding their own business. The lady in the coach is not connected to them at all.
points: **He announces it to Sancho as fact.**
**He attacks anyway** and knocks a monk off his mule.
**The monks are wearing travelling masks** against the dust.

cards.title: The squire helps himself to the spoils
cards.text: Sancho begins stripping the fallen monk of his clothes, on the grounds that spoils belong to the victor.
points: **He has learned the rules of chivalry** selectively.
**The monks' servants beat him for it.**
**Nobody in this scene** comes out well.
**Cervantes is laughing at both of them.**

question.text: What does Don Quixote believe the monks are doing?
options: Carrying off a princess by force
Racing him to the next town
question.explain: He decides they are enchanters abducting a princess. They are two travellers on mules.

terms.def: The base form of the verb, with -s or -es for he, she and it.
He, she or it. The only form that changes in the simple present.
Something always true. Water boils at 100 °C.
Something done regularly. He trains every morning.
A helper verb. Do and does form negatives and questions.
Goods taken from a defeated enemy. Sancho claims the monk's clothes as these.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Only he, she and it take -s or -es.**
**After do or does**, the main verb loses the -s.

options: She goes to school by bus
She go to school by bus
She gos to school by bus
She going to school by bus
quiz.explain: Go ends in -o, so it takes -es. She, he and it are the only forms that change.
quiz.objective: Form the simple present tense, including the third person singular

quiz.text: Write the third person singular of "fix".
quiz.objective: Apply the spelling rules for adding -s or -es

quiz.text: What is the third person singular of "carry"?
quiz.explain: There is a consonant before the y, so the y becomes i and -es is added.
quiz.objective: Apply the spelling rules for adding -s or -es

quiz.text: What is the third person singular of "enjoy"?
quiz.explain: There is a vowel before the y, so the y stays and you just add -s.
quiz.objective: Apply the spelling rules for adding -s or -es

quiz.text: "Water freezes at 0 °C." Which use of the simple present is this?
quiz.explain: Always true, regardless of when you say it. That is a general truth.
quiz.objective: Explain the four main uses of the simple present

quiz.text: "He shoots, he scores!" Which use is this?
quiz.explain: Live commentary uses the simple present, which is why it feels immediate.
quiz.objective: Explain the four main uses of the simple present

quiz.text: "The film starts at eight." Which use is this?
quiz.explain: English uses the simple present for fixed timetables, even for a future event.
quiz.objective: Explain the four main uses of the simple present

quiz.text: What does Don Quixote take the two monks to be?
quiz.explain: They are travellers on mules. The lady in the coach behind them is nothing to do with them.
quiz.objective: Retell the episode with the monks and the coach

quiz.text: What does Sancho do after the monk falls?
options: He starts taking the monk's clothes as spoils
He helps the monk back onto his mule
quiz.explain: He has picked up the rules of chivalry selectively. The monks' servants beat him for it.
quiz.objective: Retell the episode with the monks and the coach

quiz.text: Sancho warns Don Quixote before he attacks the monks.
quiz.explain: True, as he did at the windmills. It makes no difference either time.
quiz.objective: Retell the episode with the monks and the coach

teacher.summary: Week 8 English covers the simple present alongside the episode with the monks, matching the Term 1 weekly scope. The forming half is a spelling topic more than a grammar one, and the verbEndings figure carries the six rules so the cards can spend their space on the y rule, which is the one that separates learning from guessing. The four uses are given equal weight because students reliably know two of them and have never noticed the other two — commentary and timetables — even though they meet both daily. The do/does card targets the double-ending error, which survives well past this age group. NOTE ON THE TEXT: the school's edition is abridged and does not follow Cervantes' chapter numbering, so this lesson follows the episode named in the title.
discussion: Put a match on mute and have him commentate for thirty seconds. Every verb will come out in the simple present without being told.
Ask why 'she doesn't likes' is wrong. One word carries the ending, and naming that fixes it permanently.
Ask him to read a game tooltip aloud and name the tense. Tooltips are general truths, and that is why they read as rules.
Ask whether anybody in the monks episode behaves well. Sancho is as ridiculous as his master here, on purpose.
teacher.extension: Have him write six tooltips for imaginary items, all in the simple present. Getting the third person -s right six times in a row is the exercise.
misconceptions: 'All verbs add -s in the present tense.' Only he, she and it change at all.
'Every -y becomes -ies.' Only after a consonant. Play becomes plays, not playies.
'Doesn't likes is more emphatic.' It is wrong. Does already carries the ending.
'The simple present is only for now.' It also covers habits, general truths and fixed timetables.
